title: Ratiometric transcriptional activation by protein degradation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data file exists to open. I retrieved the open bioRxiv preprint full text (PMC13228303, licence CC BY-NC-ND) and read its data-availability statement: 'All data are available in the main text or the supplementary materials.' Its only supplementary item is 'Supplement 1 = Materials and Methods, Figures S1-S7, Supplementary References' - zero data tables; the text contains no 'Table S', no 'Data S', no 'SMILES'. I searched for deposited data and found none: no GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) / SRA (Sequence Read Archive) / BioProject links from PubMed ID 42679820, 0 hits on Zenodo, 0 on Dryad, 0 on DataCite, figshare API returned an error. Europe PMC's supplementary-file endpoint returned a 230-byte non-zip stub and the direct preprint PDF supplement returned HTTP 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All numbers quoted here come from the preprint text, not from files: a 7,479-molecule clinical compound collection screened against four RTA (ratiometric transcriptional activation) reporter cell lines (MYC, STAT3, FOXP3, SHP2), a custom 920-molecule CRBN (Cereblon, an E3 ubiquitin ligase substrate receptor) library screened against CK1-alpha, UBE2S, FOXP3 and MYC, a 5-cell-line barcoded pool, and 12 monoclonal reporter lines. A web search snippet of the paywalled Cell page listed supplemental items Data S4 (mathematical modelling), Data S5 (plasmid sequences), Data S6 (NMR spectrum), Data S7 (FASTQ reads for Figures 5J-5L) and Data S8 (flow-cytometry gating) - I could not open that page (no publisher scraping) and could not confirm any compound-level results table.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified. The Cell article and its supplement are subscription-only; the open preprint's single supplement is a methods/figures PDF that Europe PMC serves with HTTP 403. No accession, no Zenodo/Dryad/DataCite/figshare deposit, no GEO/SRA link from the PubMed record. The screen results exist only as plotted points in figures.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The candidate label (percent reporter-positive cells per compound) is not in any released column; it would have to be reconstructed from scatter-plot images in Figures 7E-7I, which is image digitisation, not a dataset.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. Even if the screen values were released, the compounds are described only as a 'clinical collection' and a 'custom CRBN-targeting library'; no SMILES (chemical structure strings) and no compound identifiers are provided anywhere in the open text.

a4_units_stated.note: Not reached in files, but the paper's readouts are clearly defined (percent mKate2-positive and GFP-positive cells, fold change versus DMSO, EC50/DC50 in nM). Units are the one thing that is unambiguous.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unverifiable. Paper text implies ~7,479 compounds x 4 reporter lines (~30,000 wells) plus 920 x 4, which would be enough - but not one of those rows is downloadable, so the count cannot be checked.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <10 MB if a screen table ever appears
a6_fits_laptop.note: A plate-level screen table would be a few megabytes; size was never the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare: there is no download to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle - the readout is a live-cell fluorescence measurement on a 384-well plate, not another model's output and not computable from chemical features. This is the one killer the project would have passed.

existing_models.name: Proteochemometric machine-learning models for Cereblon (CRBN) glue activity (published in a Elsevier computational-chemistry journal; seen only as a search result title and snippet, full text not retrieved)
existing_models.score_and_split: Snippet reports 89% of per-target models above 0.8 ROC-AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) and 70% above 0.2 MCC (Matthews correlation coefficient) on primary screening data; split not stated in the snippet.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Snippet frames target selectivity and compound prioritisation as the remaining challenge; I did not read the discussion.

existing_models.name: Interpretable ML on integrated CRBN degrader proteomics ('Integrated proteomic screening reveals design principles of CRBN molecular glue degraders', bioRxiv 2026; seen only as a search result)
existing_models.score_and_split: Snippet reports chemical fingerprints driving neosubstrate selectivity for CSNK1A1, ZFP91 and WEE1; no metric or split retrieved.

backbone.name: ChemBERTa or MolFormer (chemical language models over SMILES strings)
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would suffice for ~8,000 molecules

integration.partner_dataset: ChEMBL / PubChem for the clinical compound collection; PROTAC-DB or the published CRBN degradation proteomics sets for degrader labels
integration.join_key: InChIKey or compound name resolved to InChIKey
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Would be: do chemical features that predict Cereblon glue activity in proteomics transfer to a transcriptional reporter readout? - but the join cannot start because this paper releases no compound list.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the known CK1-alpha CRBN glues and the macrolides (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus, ascomycin) that the paper reports as top MYC hits; the model must rank these highly.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling and the FOXP3 reporter line, which the authors themselves use as a non-specific-activation control.
controls.external_validation: Published CRBN degradation proteomics datasets would serve, but no shared compound identifiers are released to join on.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: with no released per-compound measurements and no compound structures, a model cannot be trained or evaluated on this paper's data at all.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a drug's chemical structure to predict whether it lowers the level of a chosen cancer protein inside living cells
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would train on each screened molecule's chemical structure (a SMILES string, the standard text encoding of a molecule) paired with its readout in four reporter cell lines. The paper describes 7,479 clinical molecules plus a 920-molecule Cereblon-targeted library, but zero of those rows are downloadable, so the usable count is 0.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be the fraction of reporter cells that light up for a given target protein, a direct live-cell fluorescence measurement on 384-well plates read by automated confocal microscopy, which rises when the target protein is destabilised.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Targeted-protein-degradation chemists (for example the Gray, Banik and Corsello labs at Stanford) would use such a model to pre-rank which library members to test for a new, never-degraded target, saving whole screening campaigns. As it stands nothing can be learned, because the measurements were never released.

more_or_better_data.why: Our usable data is zero released rows; the existing Cereblon glue machine-learning work was trained on hundreds of internal screening campaigns across thousands of compounds. We have nothing to bring.

confidence_score.why: The paper reports triplicate measurements and Z'-scores, which would support a noise estimate, but none of the replicate values are released, so no per-prediction confidence can be calibrated.

models_beatable.why: The named Cereblon models are recent (2024-2026) and their training data is proprietary pharma screening data, which keeps the open problem open - but that is irrelevant without any data on our side.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Every condition fails: we cannot run their model, we have no training rows, no shared compound identifiers to join on, and no split to evaluate on.

label_elsewhere.sources: Not assessed - the candidate was rejected at Part A1, so no public-resource search for this label was carried out.
label_elsewhere.join_key: InChIKey (would be needed, but no compound identifiers are released)
label_elsewhere.why: Nothing follows from the label's availability elsewhere when this paper contributes no joinable rows.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: predict per-target protein-destabilisation activity (percent reporter-positive cells) from molecular structure using a frozen chemical language model (ChemBERTa) plus a small regression head, trained across the four RTA reporter lines so that target-specific and non-specific (FOXP3 control line) activity can be separated. The idea is sound and the readout is a genuine physical measurement, but the paper releases no compound list, no structures and no screen values, so there is no feature table to build.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data to load. A ~8,000-molecule ChemBERTa embedding job would be well under an hour on a laptop CPU if the compound list ever became available.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the data-availability statement and the supplementary file list and ask 'is there a table with one row per screened compound?' - 10 minutes, and it killed this candidate.

verdict_reason: No data released anywhere: screen results exist only inside figures of a paywalled paper.
